result.notes:
Both defects are real; both reproduced independently before any edit (script: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/fix_WP10/repro.py), both fixed, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-fix source.

DEFECT 1 (alphasage._unroll looks up a FeatureToken for a daily leaf) -- CONFIRMED, FIXED.
Reproduced at three depths with Vocabulary(default_registry(), daily_fields=('FloatCap',)): _unroll, build_partial_tree_graph, and GFlowNetSampler.sample(greedy=True) with the policy's output bias nudged toward the daily token all died with KeyError "token FeatureToken(field='FloatCap') is not in the vocabulary". The root cause is exactly as reported: `fields` and `daily_fields` are parallel namespaces in Vocabulary (tokens.py:110 vs :118), so a vocabulary carrying DailyFeatureToken('FloatCap') never carries FeatureToken('FloatCap') -- there is no vocabulary shape on which the old line both works and has daily tokens. Fixed by `nodes.append(vocab.index_of(DailyFeatureToken(expr.field)))`, the exact inverse of ExpressionBuilder.push's DailyFeatureToken branch, with the stale WP4 comment replaced by one explaining the namespace split and why GFlowNetSampler.sample (which rebuilds the graph from the whole stack at the top of every step) makes a stale lookup fatal one step after the first daily draw. I confirmed _unroll is the only leaf->token lookup in src: `grep -rn FeatureToken src/` shows only tokens.py's own definitions/uses and these two alphasage lines.
The reported hole in the WP4 test is also real and is why the suite stayed green: test_daily_leaf_engine.py:462 built Vocabulary(registry, fields=list(registry.fields) + ['FloatCap']) -- a minute field named 'FloatCap', which WP10 cannot produce -- so the test asserting "_unroll is correct given ANY vocabulary that carries a token for the field (however WP10 arranges for that)" asserted nothing about the real path. Repointed at daily_fields=['FloatCap'] / DailyFeatureToken, with an added `assert FeatureToken('FloatCap') not in vocab.token_to_index` so the fixture can never silently drift back to a shape that cannot occur. Its sibling at :447 (KeyError naming FloatCap on a daily-free vocabulary) passes unchanged -- after the fix it raises on DailyFeatureToken instead, which still matches.
New tests in tests/test_daily_tokens.py: test_alphasage_state_graph_resolves_a_daily_leaf_on_a_wp10_vocabulary (bare leaf, then under cs_rank, with the stack re-read from scratch each time, pinning node_token_idx/root_ids/edges/n_pending_windows) and test_gflownet_sampler_draws_a_daily_token_and_keeps_going (end to end: daily-token bias 50, SEP bias 100, greedy -> n_steps == 2, expr.key() == 'DF:FloatCap', is_valid_root). The second one covers the actual crash path, the step after the daily token enters the stack. Both import alphasage locally so the module's import path stays torch-free.

DEFECT 2 (non-finite op_weight becomes a NaN/inf bias) -- CONFIRMED, FIXED.
Reproduced: max(float('nan'), 1e-9) is nan in Python (max returns its first argument unless the second compares greater), so op_weight returning NaN wrote np.float64(nan) into the bias array, and +inf wrote inf. The downstream consequence reproduced too: adding that row to flat logits makes torch.distributions.Categorical(logits=...) raise ValueError about the Real() constraint, naming no operator and no field. The asymmetry with the GP arm reproduced as well -- TypedTreeGenerator(reg, op_weight=<NaN for day_mean>) raises "op_weight for 'day_mean' must be a finite float >= 0, got nan" at construction, and generator._pick_weighted's max(0.0, nan) == 0.0 silently drops the operator. So the design's "one shared op_weight then steers both searches" really did give one arm a silent drop and the other an opaque late crash. Fixed by validating `math.isfinite(w)` per operator and raising ValueError naming the operator, with the docstring now stating both halves of the contract (non-finite rejected, negative floored, and why each). -inf is rejected along with nan/+inf even though max(-inf, tiny) happened to produce a finite log(tiny): a non-finite weight is an upstream bug the GP arm already refuses, and letting it through quietly would re-create exactly the divergence this fix removes.
New tests: test_operator_logit_bias_rejects_a_non_finite_weight_naming_the_operator (parametrized over nan/inf/-inf, asserting the operator name is in the message) and test_operator_logit_bias_stays_finite_for_every_token_under_extreme_weights (the array a caller receives is always finite, so adding it to a logit row cannot introduce a NaN/inf of its own -- this one is an invariant pin, not a regression test; it passes pre-fix too).
